taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-10, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 104.3 | 6.31 | 6.31
2 | 416.7 | 17.57 | 23.88
3 | 264.5 | 2.29 | 26.17
4 | 856.9 | 2.63 | 28.80
5 | 641.5 | 26.88 | 55.68
6 | 7698.1 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as A-type.

Is this label correct for these layer values? Give a short answer, then end with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"label_correct": true or false, "curve_type": "<letters>"}

The curve-type notation is determined by analyzing groups of three consecutive layer resistivities. For the given resistivities:

1.  **Layer 1-2-3:** 104.3, 416.7, 264.5. Since 104.3 < 416.7 and 416.7 > 264.5, this is a **K** type.
2.  **Layer 2-3-4:** 416.7, 264.5, 856.9. Since 416.7 > 264.5 and 264.5 < 856.9, this is an **H** type.
3.  **Layer 3-4-5:** 264.5, 856.9, 641.5. Since 264.5 < 856.9 and 856.9 > 641.5, this is a **K** type.
4.  **Layer 4-5-6:** 856.9, 641.5, 7698.1. Since 856.9 > 641.5 and 641.5 < 7698.1, this is an **H** type.

Combining these, the curve-type notation for 6 layers is KHKH. The file's classification of "A-type" is incorrect.

{"label_correct": false, "curve_type": "KHKH"}
